message: Operation 'getCompanyDetails' has semantic quality issues: vague_summary, missing_context. Summary 'Get company details' is too generic and doesn't convey the richness of the response (leadership, corporate relationships, hiring data). The description is exceptionally comprehensive, covering all response fields, edge cases (subdomain resolution, missing hiring data), and credit model. Improved summary highlights the key data categories (leadership, relationships, hiring) to help AI agents understand the operation's scope and value.

data.current_description:
Full detail payload for one company, addressed by domain — the public identifier returned by search, lookup, and similar results. `company` carries the canonical profile (including `defunct`); `people` lists cofounders and C-suite/execs with role, LinkedIn URL, and prior companies (each prior company includes a `domain` you can feed back into this endpoint to walk the graph). `leadership_data` reports coverage: `available`, `not_available` (company known, but not in the leadership subset — most companies), or `error` (transient lookup failure).

When the company has known ownership edges, the payload also carries a `relationships` block (key absent otherwise): `parents` (all direct parents with their `relation`), `ultimate_parent` and `lineage` (ordered root → immediate parent; both null/empty when ownership is ambiguous, e.g. joint ventures — fall back to `parents`), and `children` grouped by relation category (`subsidiary`, `product_of`, `joint_venture`, `merger`, `other`). Child lists are complete — never truncated. Every related company includes a `domain`; feed it back into this endpoint to walk the corporate family. `source` reports the edges' provenance (e.g. `analyst_curated`) and is present when all edges share one origin.

When we hold job-board data for the company, `company.hiring` carries its current openings: `active_job_count` (total open roles), `has_remote_job`, and three ranked breakdowns of `{name, count}` — `by_department` (up to 15), `by_country` (up to 10, country names rather than ISO2 codes) and `by_city` (up to 5). It comes from a weekly scrape of the company's own job board and counts active postings only.

`hiring` is **absent** when we hold no posting data, which is not the same as the company not hiring — coverage is roughly 20,000 companies. Treat a missing block as "no data", never as "no open roles". The breakdowns are ranked top-Ns for display, not complete sets (the largest company in the data posts across 3,371 distinct cities) — to FILTER on hiring, use the `jobs` filters on `POST /api/v1/search`, which match against the full lists.

A subdomain resolves through its **registered domain** when only the parent is a known company: `coilcoatings.akzonobel.com` returns AkzoNobel. The response then carries `requested_domain`, `matched_domain` and `resolved_via: "registered_domain"`, and the profile is the PARENT company's — check `relationships.children` for the specific unit. All three keys are absent when the requested domain resolved exactly.

**Credits:** 1, charged only when the domain resolves to a real company — a 404 is free.

**MCP twin:** `get_company_details`.

data.current_description:
Full detail payload for one company, addressed by domain — the public identifier returned by search, lookup, and similar results. `company` carries the canonical profile (including `defunct`); `people` lists cofounders and C-suite/execs with role, LinkedIn URL, and prior companies (each prior company includes a `domain` you can feed back into this endpoint to walk the graph). `leadership_data` reports coverage: `available`, `not_available` (company known, but not in the leadership subset — most companies), or `error` (transient lookup failure).

When the company has known ownership edges, the payload also carries a `relationships` block (key absent otherwise): `parents` (all direct parents with their `relation`), `ultimate_parent` and `lineage` (ordered root → immediate parent; both null/empty when ownership is ambiguous, e.g. joint ventures — fall back to `parents`), and `children` grouped by relation category (`subsidiary`, `product_of`, `joint_venture`, `merger`, `other`). Child lists are complete — never truncated. Every related company includes a `domain`; feed it back into this endpoint to walk the corporate family. `source` reports the edges' provenance (e.g. `analyst_curated`) and is present when all edges share one origin.

When we hold job-board data for the company, `company.hiring` carries its current openings: `active_job_count` (total open roles), `has_remote_job`, and three ranked breakdowns of `{name, count}` — `by_department` (up to 15), `by_country` (up to 10, country names rather than ISO2 codes) and `by_city` (up to 5). It comes from a weekly scrape of the company's own job board and counts active postings only.

`hiring` is **absent** when we hold no posting data, which is not the same as the company not hiring — coverage is roughly 20,000 companies. Treat a missing block as "no data", never as "no open roles". The breakdowns are ranked top-Ns for display, not complete sets (the largest company in the data posts across 3,371 distinct cities) — to FILTER on hiring, use the `jobs` filters on `POST /api/v1/search`, which match against the full lists.

A subdomain resolves through its **registered domain** when only the parent is a known company: `coilcoatings.akzonobel.com` returns AkzoNobel. The response then carries `requested_domain`, `matched_domain` and `resolved_via: "registered_domain"`, and the profile is the PARENT company's — check `relationships.children` for the specific unit. All three keys are absent when the requested domain resolved exactly.

**Credits:** 1, charged only when the domain resolves to a real company — a 404 is free.

**MCP twin:** `get_company_details`.
